title: ICON 1.5 — Combat
description: How a fight runs in the ICON combat tracker: alternating turns, activations, slow turns, Resolve and statuses.

steps.title: Combat in ICON
steps.content:
ICON has no initiative. A player character always goes first (the players choose who), then the GM picks a foe, then a player again, and so on, alternating (p.87).
The tracker follows this for you. The tour is clearer with a combat already started, but it works without one too.

steps.title: The tracker
steps.content: Add tokens to combat from their token HUD, then Begin Combat. Every combatant is a row; the ones who still have to act are on top, the spent ones at the bottom.

steps.title: Round, side and Party Resolve
steps.content: The banner shows the round and whose side picks next (PC PICKS NEXT / NPC PICKS NEXT). Party Resolve goes up by 1 at the start of each round and empties when combat ends (p.99); − / + adjust it by hand.

steps.title: Taking a turn
steps.content:
Each row has one pip per activation left: click a pip to start that character's turn, and the stop button to end it.
Foes and legends with several activations get several pips. The GM's right-click menu can add, remove or undo an activation.

steps.title: Slow turns
steps.content: A player can skip their turn and take a slow turn later in the round instead. ⏸ Slow marks it, and the character moves after the normal turns.

steps.title: Statuses on the selected token
steps.content:
Select a token that has statuses and a panel opens at the top right, next to the sidebar, listing them in large type.
On tokens you own you can adjust stacks (Blessed, power dice, Vigilance, Elevation) with − / + and remove a status with ×.

steps.title: Attack, damage, Apply
steps.content: Target the enemies, then roll from the sheet. The attack card checks each target's Defense; the damage card has Apply and half buttons for each target, with Armor, Vigor, Cover and Resistance worked out on the spot. Statuses an ability inflicts get their own buttons on the card.
